title: Katie Boulter Wins After a Rain Delay in Japan
summary:
British tennis player Katie Boulter won her first match at the Japan Open in Osaka. But she had to wait until the next day to finish it.

Boulter played Himeno Sakatsume, a Japanese player the home crowd cheered for. On Monday, Boulter won the first set and was ahead 3-1 in the second set. Then rain stopped the match.

On Tuesday, the players came back. Boulter won 6-3, 6-1.

"Yesterday was a tough spot to end at," Boulter said. She said she had to keep the same focus the next day to finish the match. She was happy she did not have to play a third set.

Boulter, who is 30, will play Viktorija Golubic of Switzerland next.

In other tennis news, star player Iga Swiatek left a different tournament because of a thigh injury. That could make it harder for her to reach the WTA Finals in November.
why_it_matters: Boulter shows that staying focused after a break can help you finish what you started, whether in sports or schoolwork.
